subject: Immediate: Dedicated GPU pool constriction impacting Sierra Systems - reserved throughput shortfall
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@sierrasys.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Sierra Systems Engineering <ops@sierra-systems.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@sierrasys.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Sierra] Production inference latency + errors — reserved capacity not meeting SLA

Diego / Redwood team,

We started a high-volume batch at 07:55 PT and within ten minutes saw median tail latency climb to ~2.4s (baseline ~350ms) and a 5xx spike across the service. Our dashboards (attached) show reserved throughput consumption dropping to ~48% of committed QPS while client-side queues and retries skyrocket. This is directly impacting customer-facing flows — several users reported timeouts.

Key info:
- Customer: Sierra Systems (production)
- Environment: us-west-2 (dedicated pool, reserved capacity)
- Observed at~: 07:58–08:05 PT
- Impact: increased latency, 5xx errors, backlog on our side

We need:
1) Immediate confirmation that this is an internal capacity issue (is the dedicated pool saturated?)
2) Short-term mitigation (burst authorization or failover) — we need this live while we investigate root cause
3) ETA on remediation and whether we should expect degraded throughput for the rest of the day

Attaching the perf CSV with the time window and a short log dump. Can you confirm and advise ASAP? We have executives asking.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Cho
Sierra Systems — Head of Integrations

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@sierrasys.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Sierra] Production inference latency + errors — reserved capacity not meeting SLA

Daniel — thanks for the data, and sorry for the disruption. We're on it. Quick update:

- I've opened a PagerDuty incident PD-9923 and the infra on-call is investigating kernel-level queueing on the dedicated GPU farm that serves this pool.
- Preliminary signal: high prefix cache churn and a sudden, co-located spike from another tenant caused scheduling pressure. That appears to have triggered our autoscaling backoff for the reserved class.

Immediate asks for you: can you confirm whether the batch that started at 07:55 included longer-than-usual sequences (>1024 tokens) or more frequent tool-calls? That helps narrow the KV-cache behavior.

I've attached a short service log extract (svc_logs_snippet.txt). I'll loop in Irene to check reservation routing and Marissa to coordinate any customer-level credits if we need to offer remediation.

Short-term plan (next 60–90 min):
- Temporarily authorize a controlled burst from the dedicated spare pool to add headroom (Irene — can you start a burst now if we approve?)
- Apply request shaping rules for Sierra to reduce tail latency while we probe root cause
- If the burst is not available, execute controlled fallback to hosted-compatible model variant to preserve availability

I'll update in 30 minutes.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: Dedicated pool saturation — immediate mitigation and exec sync

Team — escalating given Sierra's execs are pressing for answers. Summary and proposed actions below.

Observed (07:55–08:08 PT):
- Dedicated pool serving Sierra saw token service loops that drove GPU queue depth to 92% across two racks.
- Reserved throughput reported to Sierra (committed QPS) fell to ~48% due to scheduler backoff; customer observed client retries and 5xx rates jumped to 0.9% from baseline 0.03%.
- Concurrent noisy neighbor identified (tenant id masked) — appears to be serving larger context windows which forced KV cache thrashing.

Immediate mitigations (please action in priority order):
1) Authorize burst to Dedicated Spares: Irene — request authorization to pull +25% headroom for Sierra (manual override). If you confirm, I'll send the customer a short note.
2) Apply per-route shaping: Marissa — please prepare an L2 customer-facing note that says we are applying shaping and will honor credits if SLA impact is confirmed. Draft attached.
3) Fallback plan: Jonas — can we approve temporary routing to hosted-compat model variant for up to 2 hours if burst fails? This preserves availability but may change output characteristics; need exec sign-off.
4) Post-incident: operations to root-cause noisy neighbor and consider stronger partitioning or reservation enforcement.

Metrics and links: hubspot deal DEAL-45872, PD-9923 incident. Raw perf CSV attached.

Proposed customer wording (short):
"We identified internal scheduling pressure impacting your dedicated pool. We've applied a temporary shaping policy and authorized additional headroom. We will follow up with a post-incident summary and an offer of credit for the affected window"

Please reply with approvals ASAP. Exec wants a four-line status for 09:30 PT.

— Diego

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@sierrasys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Sierra] Production inference latency + errors — dedicated pool remediations in place

Daniel — short update and concrete next steps.

What we observed:
- A co-located tenant created KV-cache pressure that led our scheduler to throttle reserved workloads; that reduced reported reserved throughput to ~48% for the window you flagged.

Actions we've taken (completed):
- Increased dedicated headroom by +25% from the spare pool (manual override) — this removed immediate queueing pressure.
- Applied per-route shaping on Sierra's production route to limit burstiness and reduce tail latency.
- Opened PD-9923 and allocated an on-call infra engineer to run a post-mortem.

Customer impact and compensation:
- We expect latency to return to baseline (350–450ms) within 10–15 minutes of the headroom change — monitoring shows improvement already.
- Marissa will follow up with a proposed credit (draft attached) for the affected window per our SLA.

Next steps:
- Ops will investigate noisy neighbor and recommend stronger VM/GPU partitioning or stricter reservation enforcement.
- We'll share a post-incident summary with root cause, timeline, and remediation within 72 hours.
- If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute bridge this afternoon (15:00 PT) to walk through details with our infra and product leads.

Attachments: sierra-inference-metrics.csv, svc_logs_snippet.txt, draft_credit_note.pdf

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate the urgency and will make this right.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0192
